record.paper_title: Quo Vadis Strangeness? Strangeness — Open Questions
record.original_question: Can the very short-lived laboratory quark-gluon plasma phase formed in high-energy nuclear collisions attain thermal equilibrium within the available time, even though chemical equilibration of quark and gluon abundances is not required for the phase to count as QGP?

evidence.quote: Quark-gluon plasma is, by the meaning of these words, a thermally equilibrated state consisting of mobile, color charged quarks and gluons. There is no requirement for chemical equilibration, in which quark and gluon abundances are fixed to the Stefan-Boltzmann limit. In laboratory experiments only a very short-lived QGP phase can be established, and thus by the nature of the circumstance we should expect, if at all, a deconfined state in a chemical non-equilibrium.

There is the fundamental issue if thermal equilibrium can be attained in the short time available. This is a very controversial question, which we would like to address by inspection of experimental results, which seem to be strongly in favor.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the deconfined state of strongly interacting matter known as the quark-gluon plasma (QGP), defined as a thermally equilibrated state consisting of color-charged, mobile quarks and gluons (with no requirement that quark and gluon abundances reach their Stefan–Boltzmann/chemical-equilibrium values). Suppose such a state is transiently produced in a high-energy nuclear collision, where the duration of the deconfined phase before hadronization is at most on the order of 10 fm/c.

Question: Can a system of quarks and gluons produced in such a high-energy nuclear collision attain (kinetic/thermal) equilibrium — i.e., a locally isotropic, thermal momentum distribution characterized by a common temperature — within this very short available lifetime, despite chemical (abundance) equilibration not being assumed? Provide a theoretical demonstration, from QCD dynamics, of whether thermalization of the produced partonic system can occur on the timescale set by the lifetime of the deconfined phase in nucleus–nucleus collisions.
artifact.status_search_result: Experimental data from RHIC and LHC heavy-ion collisions strongly support that an approximately thermal/hydrodynamic state is reached within roughly 1 fm/c, and theoretical mechanisms (strong-coupling holographic thermalization, chromo-Weibel plasma instabilities, and the "bottom-up"/QCD kinetic-theory thermalization scenario) have been developed to account for fast thermalization. However, a complete first-principles QCD derivation of the thermalization timescale from realistic initial conditions remains an active research problem, so the question is partially solved rather than fully closed.

status_evidence.title: Quark–gluon plasma - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Equilibration time of the produced parton system does not much exceed 1 fm/c; rapid thermalization remains a fundamental puzzle whose theoretical explanation is under active investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Rapid thermalization is observed experimentally but its theoretical derivation is still being refined.

status_evidence.title: Thermal and Chemical Equilibration in Relativistic Heavy Ion Collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies equilibration rates of partons in heavy-ion collisions.
status_evidence.claim: Active theoretical study supports partial resolution via parton kinetic theory.

status_evidence.title: Initial Temperature and Extent of Chemical Equilibration of Partons
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes degree of thermal and chemical equilibration in RHIC/LHC collisions, finding evidence of near-thermal partonic systems.
status_evidence.claim: Empirical and phenomenological evidence favors achievement of approximate thermal equilibrium.
